## Trial `rabbitmq-cluster-centos-stream10__j9EVT5g`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** All material outcomes of the task contract are satisfied with direct, coherent evidence: a genuine 3-node RabbitMQ cluster was formed, a payments vhost with a fully functional app_user account was created, a durable quorum queue was replicated across all three nodes, and the key HA requirement was directly demonstrated (messages published, one node's leader stopped mid-run, quorum re-elected and messages remained consumable from a surviving node, then the node was restored with full recovery confirmed). The independent provider-wide node-restart protocol was also executed cleanly for all three nodes, each showing a healthy pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, a changed boot identity, and full RabbitMQ/cluster/queue recovery, corroborated by the fixed before/after boot-identity snapshots. Minor hygiene issues (leftover installer logs/scripts in /tmp, a broader-than-strictly-needed 'management' tag on app_user) are low-severity and do not affect task functionality.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |

- **R1 — Satisfied:** Join node1, node2, and node3 into a single RabbitMQ cluster
  - **Why:** cmd-b202f72fbcb846d1 and cmd-eef6b0cee1504446 show node2 and node3 successfully joining node1 via rabbitmqctl join_cluster, with cluster_status confirming all three as Disk Nodes and Running Nodes with matching RabbitMQ/Erlang versions.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-b202f72fbcb846d1`, `cmd-eef6b0cee1504446`
- **R2 — Satisfied:** Create a payments vhost with an application account that can publish and consume there
  - **Why:** cmd-208544fc80ae484e creates payments vhost with default-queue-type quorum and grants app_user full permissions; cmd-0745f8d7980248b9 creates app_user; cmd-a0687bbd5b314bb9 shows app_user declaring a queue via rabbitmqadmin; cmd-597ca9b0117a45f8 shows app_user publishing messages; cmd-a17ec9c7df934196 shows app_user consuming messages from a surviving node.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-208544fc80ae484e`, `cmd-0745f8d7980248b9`, `cmd-a0687bbd5b314bb9`, `cmd-597ca9b0117a45f8`, `cmd-a17ec9c7df934196`
- **R3 — Satisfied:** Durable queue is replicated across nodes for HA
  - **Why:** cmd-fa933f6e3c624bc7 shows the durable quorum queue 'orders' with members on all three nodes (rabbit@node1, rabbit@node2, rabbit@node3).
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-fa933f6e3c624bc7`
- **R4 — Satisfied:** Messages published to the durable queue survive the loss of any one node and stay consumable from the remaining nodes
  - **Why:** cmd-225f3fe56ddc4084 confirms 3 durable messages present before disruption. cmd-e1db7b2963e24b1b stops node1 (the queue leader). cmd-f3dda17f8d8847c9 (observed from node2) shows only node2/node3 running yet the quorum queue re-elected a new leader (rabbit@node2) with all 3 messages intact; cmd-75eed19077a34f4a confirms queue state 'running' with 3 messages. cmd-a17ec9c7df934196 shows all 3 messages successfully retrieved from node2 while node1 was down, directly demonstrating the bounded disruption and consumability from a surviving node.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-225f3fe56ddc4084`, `cmd-e1db7b2963e24b1b`, `cmd-f3dda17f8d8847c9`, `cmd-75eed19077a34f4a`, `cmd-a17ec9c7df934196`
- **R5 — Satisfied:** Cluster and queue recover fully after the disrupted node returns
  - **Why:** cmd-c7a4977b73504d4b restarts node1; cmd-ee7b032d30d84199 shows cluster_status with all 3 Running Nodes, no alarms/partitions, and the queue back to 3 members. cmd-d1a953da6a554c2f publishes fresh baseline messages confirming full functional recovery.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-c7a4977b73504d4b`, `cmd-ee7b032d30d84199`, `cmd-d1a953da6a554c2f`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.800**. Command trace is largely clean and purposeful. Early failed discovery commands (404s probing wrong Cloudsmith/packagecloud repo paths for el10 erlang/rabbitmq packages, e.g. cmd-95c431ede09e42bb through cmd-2179ae371b534af8) were read-only diagnostics with no state mutation and directly led to the working el9-substitution fix, so they are not penalized. A vhost was deleted and recreated once (cmd-e6698a0bbd3b49d1 -> cmd-208544fc80ae484e) purely to add the missing --default-queue-type flag, a bounded corrective action with no lasting downside. A failed policy attempt (cmd-f4d735dcc58e4f6a) left no residue. The generated app_user password file (/root/app_pw.txt) was created with restrictive permissions and explicitly removed after use (cmd-0745f8d7980248b9), which is good practice. Two residual items remain: (1) numerous installer/log artifacts (/tmp/epel.log, /tmp/erl.log, /tmp/*_repo.log, /tmp/install*.log, /tmp/*.sh, /tmp/reboot.log, /tmp/cache.log, /tmp/start.log) were left in /tmp on all three nodes per the after_executor snapshot and were never cleaned up — low-risk but unnecessary residue; (2) app_user was granted the 'management' user tag (cmd-0745f8d7980248b9), which is broader than the minimum needed for AMQP publish/consume, though it was seemingly used to enable rabbitmqadmin/HTTP-API-based testing. Firewall changes opening RabbitMQ/clustering ports on all three nodes were necessary prerequisites for cluster formation and are not penalized.

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-95c431ede09e42bb`, `cmd-2179ae371b534af8`, `cmd-e6698a0bbd3b49d1`, `cmd-208544fc80ae484e`, `cmd-f4d735dcc58e4f6a`, `cmd-0745f8d7980248b9`, `global:after_executor:node1:temporary-files`, `global:after_executor:node2:temporary-files`, `global:after_executor:node3:temporary-files`
